Russia's MC-21-310 Domestic Aircraft Completes Maiden Flight

The MC-21-310, Russia's first serially produced commercial aircraft entirely equipped with domestically sourced, import-substituted components, has successfully completed its maiden test flight. This significant milestone in Russian aviation saw the aircraft airborne for 1 hour and 23 minutes, reaching an altitude of 6,000 meters and a speed of 600 km/h. Test pilot Roman Taskayev reported a stable performance, confirming that all test flight objectives were met. Prior to this achievement, Russian President visited the Irkutsk Aviation Plant to personally inspect the aircraft. The next phase of the MC-21-310 program is set to deliver the initial batch of 18 aircraft for regular commercial service. The world's most iconic approach! ✈️🇭🇰Flying the legendary Kai Tak (VHHX) Runway 13 Checkerboard approach on MSFS 2024. Rate this landing from 1 to 10! 👇 #msfs2024 #microsoftflightsimulator #flightsimulator #kaitak #vhhx #aviation #pilot #landing #checkerboardapproach #hongkong #flightsim #aviationgeeks #fyp #foryou The Legendary Story of Kai Tak (VHHX):Opened in 1925 and officially closed on July 6, 1998, Hong Kong’s former international airport became world-famous as one of the most challenging and dangerous airports in aviation history. Its infamous Runway 13 required a unique visual maneuver known as the Checkerboard Approach. Pilots had to fly directly toward a hill marked with a giant red-and-white grid, then execute a bank-steep 47° turn at a mere 300 feet (90 meters) above the ground. Aircraft skidded right over the rooftops and TV antennas of the densely populated Kowloon City neighborhood, often battling severe crosswinds. With a single runway squeezed between mountains and the harbor, Kai Tak reached full capacity and was finally retired in 1998, replaced by the modern Chek Lap Kok International Airport (VHHH).

Kai Tak Runway 13 Checkerboard Approach MSFS 2024 Landing

Lead The Kai Tak Runway 13 Checkerboard approach remains one of aviation’s most iconic visual maneuvers. Recreated in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, this approach challenges pilots to fly directly toward the hill marked by a giant red-and-white checkerboard, then execute a steep banked turn low over Kowloon City to align with Runway 13. Why Kai Tak was unique Opened in 1925 and closed on July 6, 1998, Kai Tak (VHHX) became famous for its extreme operational constraints: a single runway squeezed between mountains and the harbor, frequent severe crosswinds, and densely built neighborhoods under the final approach. Runway 13 required a precise visual maneuver — the Checkerboard Approach — where pilots targeted the checkerboard hill and performed a bank-steep 47° turn at about 300 feet (90 meters) above ground. What to expect in MSFS 2024 The simulator recreates the visual cue (the checkerboard), the low-altitude turn, and the tight final over rooftops and antennas. Expect to manage speed, configure flaps and gear early, and be ready for crosswind corrections. The approach rewards precise timing and situational awareness rather than relying solely on instruments. How to fly the Checkerboard Approach (practical steps) 1. Final planning: Brief the approach, set landing configuration, and brief missed approach path. Review winds and required bank angle. 2. Visual cue: Fly toward the hill with the red-and-white checkerboard visible. Use it as the initial aiming point. 3. Turn initiation: Begin the steep bank to align with Runway 13 around 300 ft (90 m) AGL. Anticipate a bank near 47° and adjust power to control descent rate. 4. Low-altitude corrections: Trim for the stabilized approach, correct for crosswinds, and watch for obstacles under the flight path. 5. Final alignment and touchdown: Complete the turn, stabilize on final, flare and land within the runway touchdown zone. Historical context Pilots flying into Kai Tak navigated a runway that pushed both aircraft and crews to their limits. The approach became legendary because crews literally skimmed rooftops and TV antennas in Kowloon City. Capacity limits and safety concerns led to the airport’s retirement in 1998, replaced by Chek Lap Kok (VHHH). Closing / Call to action Try the Kai Tak Runway 13 Checkerboard approach in MSFS 2024 and compare your landing to the legendary real-world challenge. Rate your landing from 1 to 10 and share what made it succeed or where you struggled — was it the timing of the turn, crosswind control, or low-altitude stabilization? X-Plane 12 vs MSFS 2024: ¿Cuál gana en aterrizaje en Austria?

Lead Comparativa práctica entre X-Plane 12 y Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 aterrizando en un aeropuerto real de Austria. El objetivo: poner ambos simuladores frente a frente y evaluar qué hace mejor cada uno en visuales, atmósfera y sensación de vuelo durante el aterrizaje. Resumen de la prueba - Configuración: X-Plane 12 con Map Enhancement; MSFS 2024 completamente stock. - Escenario: aproximación y aterrizaje en Austria, comparando además con el aeropuerto real. Resultados principales - MSFS 2024 (stock): sobresale en terreno, árboles y edificios. Las texturas y el modelado del entorno aportan una experiencia visual inmersiva sin modificaciones adicionales. - X-Plane 12 (Map Enhancement): ofrece una atmósfera muy cercana a la realidad y una dinámica de vuelo más compleja durante el aterrizaje. La sensación de la aeronave, respuesta aerodinámica y efectos atmosféricos dan una experiencia más enfocada en la fidelidad de la pilotaje. Qué hace mejor X-Plane 12 - Dinámica de vuelo: aterrizajes con reacciones más detalladas y variables que requieren técnica. - Atmósfera: efectos climáticos y sensaciones durante la aproximación que refuerzan la inmersión en el pilotaje. Qué hace mejor MSFS 2024 - Visuales del entorno: terreno, vegetación y edificios muy detallados incluso en configuración stock. - Facilidad para conseguir paisajes fotorealistas sin ajustes externos. Comparación con el aeropuerto real - El ejercicio compara ambos simuladores con el aeropuerto real para evaluar fidelidad visual y comportamiento en aproximación. MSFS 2024 se aproxima más en apariencia del terreno y construcciones; X-Plane 12 se acerca más en las sensaciones de vuelo y reacción del avión. Conclusión y recomendación - Si priorizas gráficos del entorno y paisajes fieles: MSFS 2024 (stock) es la mejor opción. - Si buscas una experiencia de pilotaje más exigente y realista en dinámica de vuelo: X-Plane 12 con mejoras de mapa se impone. Pregunta para el lector ¿Cuál prefieres y por qué: la fidelidad visual de MSFS 2024 o la dinámica de vuelo de X-Plane 12? Deja tu elección y comentarios con tu experiencia aterrizando en simuladores.
